rows.text: The beast stirring in the darkness opens THEIR maw once more, demanding a god as a sacrifice. Before the moon rises again, only the blood of the wise can sate THEIR hunger...
So, remember what we were talking about at the end of the last chapter?
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: You can also call me...
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Aha.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: I do have many questions, but Planarcadia doesn't have that kind of time.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: So, I only have one question. If you really are Aha, you'll naturally be able to answer it.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Prove it to me.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Fair enough. I'm the one who should take the initiative.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: While the world's stereotype of the Elation doesn't usually include mind reading, I don't mind pulling a little magic trick for you.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: And as an apology for trespassing into your mind, I'll also answer those "many questions" you mentioned.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Oh? Wait, you never asked? Uh, doesn't matter. I'll just list a few.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Oh, so these are the questions you picked back then.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: For a striking opener, which question should we start with?
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Have you ever been in love?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: ...Uh? What? Who put this question in here?
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: With this option staring me right in the face, how could I not pick it?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: I already asked Asat Pramad about his love life. Now it's your turn!
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Haha, Asat Pramad's love life, huh? Oh, now that's a story...
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Don't you think the name "Dorothy" shows up a bit too often in the legends about him?
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: I'm asking you!
Nice try. But I'm asking you.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: O—Of course I've loved!
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: I can see it burning in all people, all species, and all matter, like a grand, endless firework show!
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: And Elation is simply using its very existence to passionately love everything in this universe!
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Don't try to weasel out of it!
No.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Happy now? No!
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Anyway, let's leave these kinds of questions off the table. Next!
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Alright, the groundwork is more or less in place.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Like you said, time's not exactly on our side. So let's cut straight to the chase.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: And now, it's time for the question that's been on your mind all along. I know what's been eating at you.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Here it is.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Why didn't you show up sooner?
After all those fights with them, you still haven't had your fill?
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Look, Asat Pramad might be able to answer that one, but I can't. The only thing I can give you is {RUBY_B#the Destruction}Nanook's{RUBY_E#} weakness.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: See that scar on his chest?
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Not my doing. Don't believe the rumors.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: {RUBY_B#The Destruction}Nanook's{RUBY_E#} weakness is himself. He hates his own powerlessness and how he lost his way. Even after embracing his own downfall and forsaking everything, he still couldn't change a single thing.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: This is true "Destruction." His wrath isn't just aimed at the stars, but also at himself and everything around him.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: You could totally use that to vanquish Nanook's Emanators, or even Nanook himself. But I can't promise you won't end up just like him.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: So, I'd recommend another approach instead: believe in love, hope, and courage.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: As the creator of the game, I shouldn't step in and change the rules.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: But they were playing so seriously, I just couldn't sit back and do nothing.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: You've probably seen that classic magic trick where they swap a person out, right? The assistant climbs into an empty box, then three, two, one — bam! When the box opens again, there's a completely different person inside.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Fifteen years ago, I performed the exact same trick. Except I wasn't fooling the audience, but destiny itself.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Sounds crazy, I know. But that's "imagenesis" for you: with just enough imagination, humans can accomplish a lot of things.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: I understand how you feel. Defeating the Voracity comes first. Whether you ask or not, I'll still give you the answers before we set out.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: While we still have a little time before we head out. Ask me anything you're curious about, I'll do my best to satisfy your curiosity.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: I've crossed paths with that little hacker before. Back before she joined them.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: A group of pathstriders of the Finality, trying to rewrite destiny and carving out an ending that can counteract Finality itself. As you might guess, it's never gonna be that simple.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: I've got a hunch. The one calling the shots for the Stellaron Hunters must've been through way too many failures. Failure gives you experience, but it also numbs you.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: That's why the "script" is always so precise, so sharp, so beyond question. And that, sadly, is about as far from my tastes as you can get.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: In other words, I could never join the Stellaron Hunters, nor can I figure out what they're really up to. But hey, that's not a bad thing.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: It's a fragment of the Harmony. Since you already knew that, this answer doesn't really mean much. Asat Pramad was telling the truth.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Rather than "what's special about this Stellaron," I think the better question is "who are you?"
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: But this isn't like one of those character bios at the start of a comic. You can't sum it up in just a couple of lines.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Because, just like that Stellaron, it used to be completely blank.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Completely blank?
"Used to be"?
Everything you've gained along your journey led you to make a wish upon the Stellaron, and that wish itself is the answer.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: You'll have to answer the question "Who are you?" yourself.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: So, how about another question? That one didn't count.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: With your power, you could easily suppress the husk, couldn't you?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Why set up a "reward" to lure people into this game?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Easily? Violence has never really been my style.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: When I realized that the Voracity might bring big trouble to the universe, all I could do was drag it into a "game".
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Toss {RUBY_B#the Propagation}Tayzzyronth{RUBY_E#} on {RUBY_B#the Voracity}Oroboros's{RUBY_E#} menu, then run off to the {RUBY_B#the Preservation}Amberhead{RUBY_E#} to call for backup.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: But the biggest headache was dealing with the Aeon's remains. Anyone who's killed a few Aeons knows: killing a god is easy, but burying one is a disaster.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: So I stole a potted plant from Yaoshi...
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: And that's how the Phantasmoon Games began?
Yep. Not a single bit of fun in it. And that's the real tragedy.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: What I didn't expect was that these planets would eventually develop life of their own. One of them even named its world after the "murderer": Ahatopia.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: What happened after, well, you probably already know.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Asat Pramad couldn't give you a solid answer to that one, huh?
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Good to know I'm not the only one who's totally lost here.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: So, you don't know either?
If even an Aeon can't answer it, that just means this problem's still a long way off. No need to deal with it yet.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: As for Asat Pramad's theory... I'll say it makes sense. But I know quite a few History Fictionologists, and they've got as many as sixteen different guesses about the Fourth Finality.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: People only believe what they want to believe. Asat Pramad's no different, if you ask me.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Sixteen?
Are there really that many Paths in the universe?
The most ridiculous one is the "Beauty" doomsday theory. Idrila probably died of pure rage from hearing that one.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Now you're asking the right questions! Some Paths have yet to emerge, and some have long since faded away.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: The way I see it: keep your vision broad, but your focus tight.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: A pessimist would say, "Can you believe this universe has four different doomsdays!?"
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Me? I say who's counting? The universe only ends once.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: That being said, I'd honestly prefer Elation to be on that list. At least there'd be laughter in the final moments.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: From Fulwish to Asat Pramad, crisis after crisis, problem after problem, why step up only now?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Watching the Supplicants tear each other apart, the arcadia get devoured by the husk, and me get played for a fool by the IPC...
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Did you have fun standing by and watching us struggle?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: So it is... just as I thought. And I've got an answer ready.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: [Trailblazer], I've been wanting to tell you this for ages.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: I'm sorry.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: And thank you for placing your hopes in me. But I'm afraid... I'm the Aeon of Elation.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Nanook wants to tear the universe apart, and the Amber Lord says "No way." Droidhead wants the answers to all questions, and Mythus says "Not a chance."
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: I say, "This game sucks, let's play something else," while HooH says, "For every gain, a loss. Fair trade."
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: When an Aeon meddles in the world of mortals, is it salvation or disaster? Experience has taught me more often than not, it's the latter. Whenever I plan to do something, something always "goes wrong."
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: But I like Planarcadia, I even wanted to live there. So, I played a part in this game as a "human."
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: But every show has to end. And since Oroboros isn't playing nice, I've got no choice but to take off my mask.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: I won't ask for your forgiveness. Anger, doubt, whatever you're feeling. Like every wish that never comes true, I'll take it all.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: That's what "Elation" is. The universe tells you to wear shackles. And you say, "Watch me dance", using every rattle as your backing track.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: That's all I have to say.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: As for the questions I never got to answer... and the mysteries that still remain... I'll write down every answer. Every last one is yours.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Actually, you don't need to apologize to me.
Don't try to brush it off.
Just a few minor hiccups. We can handle this ourselves.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Instead of apologizing, how about you actually do something?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: What matters is what we do next.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Planarcadia may be encanvased and sealed, but the crisis is far from over.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: So, do you have a plan?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: You must've heard that classic question: how many steps does it take to put a Nosewalker in a refrigerator?
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Similarly, how many steps does it take to suppress the Voracity?
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: First find THEM, then defeat THEM?
Open the fridge, then put THEM in?
Uh, are those two questions even related?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Find it, then defeat it. In principle, there's really no difference.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: The difference is that we need to turn every step of "finding it" into part of the Phantasmoon Games.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: When it finally reveals its true form under the spotlight, the game will reach its climax. And we'll take the Wishpower from the audience to strike the final blow.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Before that, we'll need a few reliable extras.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: After all, I'm not the only one walking the Path of Elation...
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: In the beginning, there was a single ripple.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: The beasts and swarm came in waves, and from the swirling wine in their cups, the Fools read the omens of departure.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: With my word, they made off with the Actors' gondola and hastened to the field for deicide.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: You already know how that story ended.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: The heroes, swindlers, madmen, and poets who once sailed upon this ship are long gone. And the Voracity has opened its eyes once more.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Now, it's our turn to carry this tale forward.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: By the name of Elation, I pledge to you the very same prize—
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: A performance of unparalleled absurdity.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: A drama of breathtaking twists and turns.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: We will steer the ancient gondola into the depths of the starry sea.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: In an unprecedented "Phantasmoon Games," we will reel in the hungriest, most ancient enemy of all — Oroboros!
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Reel in... the Voracity?
Is that a metaphor?
That's right. In the script of the Elation, even an Aeon is just another big catch once THEY take the bait.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Nope, I mean literally.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: In the script of the Elation, even an Aeon is just another big catch once THEY take the bait.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: As long as the bait's tempting enough, it won't be able to resist this feast.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: So, everyone, think about it: if we're throwing a grand feast, what should be on the menu?
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: The stage? The audience? The actors? Or fireworks?
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Come on, you weeping rowers!
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: I need you to row those oars and bring me that great ship capable of illuminating the stars.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Prop team, no slacking off either! Go swipe a spindle from Pteruges-V for me, and rip an anchor off Lushaka's ghost ship.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: They'll be our fishing line and hook.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Finally, as for the rest of you—
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: I want you to head to the Cavity System, brave the puffed candy storm, and find me enough candies, mousses, and chocolate bars, as well as the "Cake of God"!
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Cake... of God?
Is that also part of what it takes to hook the Voracity?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: No, I'm just a little hungry.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Once these Phantasmoon Games wrap up, we're definitely gonna need a slice of the greatest cake ever to celebrate.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Alright, folks. Let's get moving!
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: I want you to put everything on the line. Desire, reason, luck, even life itself.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: We're here to entertain the most humorless of guests, but luckily—
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: We're the universe's top experts on "Elation"!
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: The script, stage, and actors are all set, and the props are... passable, I suppose.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: But to put on the grandest show of all, it seems we still have no clue about the audience, do we?
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Old Sampo's got your back! The person you're looking for has been waiting just offstage this whole time.
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: Hehe... hello there, [Trailblazer]!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Hehe, If you're all showing off what you can do, I'm not gonna be left behind!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: You guys made way too much of a scene at the Lodestar Tower. Me and the furbos were just preparing to make a run for it when a bunch of suits suddenly barged into the newsroom and told me to come with them.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: I thought, "Oh no, I'm toast." But who knew? Then I opened a door... and well... here I am.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Ooh, sorry about that. Mourning Actors are never great with words.
rows.speaker: Sampo

rows.text: Sampo already filled me in. Go ahead, Miss Nihilux... hmm, no, Troupe Master.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: What role do you need me to play in the upcoming Phantasmoon Games?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: It takes me just two seconds of looking into someone's eyes to figure out exactly what part they were born to play.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Miss March... the role that suits you best this time is the "Diplomat."
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: D—Diplomat?
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: These Phantasmoon Games need a big enough "audience."
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: We need someone to reach out to Mr. Arita, coordinate with Sunday to reroute the Astral Express's relay signal, then get as many cameras as possible pointed at Planarcadia.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: And there's simply no one more suitable for this job than you, the quick-witted and silver-tongued Miss March 7th!
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Hehe, you've got a great eye for talent, Troupe Master!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: But... negotiating with Arita? That sounds even harder than taking on a Doomsday Beast.
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Don't worry. Sure, we owe a few favors here and there, but we've reached a temporary agreement with the IPC. Arita will give us his full support, and Sampo will also provide backup. Plus—
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: The original crew is here, ready to take your orders. Think of it as an apology.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Whoa... now I'm feeling a lot more confident!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: [Trailblazer], I'll handle the logistics. You guys do your best. See you in Planarcadia!
rows.speaker: March 7th

rows.text: Yeah, see you in Planarcadia!
So you really can tell what role someone's suited for just by looking into their eyes for two seconds?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: What role suits me best?
Your role...
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: That's a secret.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: After seeing that little scene just now, there's no doubt about who I really am, is there?
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: If anything, it's only gotten more mysterious...
Let's get to the point.
I've never seen Masked Fools so willing to do as they're told.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: You managed to make the Fools and the Actors call a historic truce. Does it really matter if I believe you?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: So, should we get going now?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Not yet. We're still missing one key piece, a MacGuffin that even the Voracity can't resist.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: To reel in a leviathan, we still need one last irresistible "bait."
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: What kind of food would the Voracity be into?
Where do we find it?
Naturally, the Voracity's favorite isn't going to be as easy to get your hands on as the "Cake of God."
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: I'm afraid only its own kind could answer that question.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: But luckily we're at the "World's End," and the last thing we're short on here is connections.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Alright, let's go. The show on stage is over. Now, it's time to take a look behind the scenes.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Let's go check the front of house first.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Two glasses of "The Last Drop of the Bomb." The usual. Put it on my tab.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: On your tab? Your tab's already stretched so thin you can't add a single drop more.
rows.speaker: Jerica

rows.text: Kiddo, don't you believe a word she says! This woman's a straight-up, no-good liar!
rows.speaker: Jerica

rows.text: A liar?
I can already tell.
Getting the truth out of this one isn't easy.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: A liar? For people in our line of work, isn't that the highest compliment?
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Allow me to present the leading star of the Mourning Actors, the sensation who set a record of thirty consecutive sold-out performances — Jerica.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: I've heard so much about you, [Trailblazer]. Of all the roles out there, yours has always been the hardest to pull off.
rows.speaker: Jerica

rows.text: This lady swore up and down that the tragicomedy she wrote for me would be a guaranteed hit. And guess what? It bombed after only seven lousy nights!
rows.speaker: Jerica

rows.text: Haha, that one was a pure accident! You know, audience tastes always change faster than the weather.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: So, let's just turn the page on that... Any word on {RUBY_B#the "bait"}what I asked for{RUBY_E#}?
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: You're actually gonna try to reel in the Voracity? I'm not about to send you to your grave.
rows.speaker: Jerica

rows.text: My, my. Look who's talking. Haven't you been itching to give this unreliable Troupe Master the boot? Well, now's your chance.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Alright. Fine. Looks like both of us just got lucky.
rows.speaker: Jerica

rows.text: You guessed right. The Fools managed to get their hands on some "classified documents" in Astropolis—
rows.speaker: Jerica

rows.text: Beneath Astropolis, in the Life Sciences Institute run by Yabuli, there's something that could make the Voracity's mouth water.
rows.speaker: Jerica

rows.text: Beneath Astropolis?
Yabuli's research institute?
Though, compared to "beneath," it's more like "beyond."
rows.speaker: Jerica

rows.text: Astropolis is shaped like a ring. On the side facing the deep black of space, there are a number of spherical modules used for special purposes. The Life Sciences Institute is one of them.
rows.speaker: Jerica

rows.text: Yep, the IPC officially calls it the "Life Sciences Institute."
rows.speaker: Jerica

rows.text: Every IPC department has placed its bets on Astropolis, and the Technology Department is no exception.
rows.speaker: Jerica

rows.text: The Life Sciences Institute, spearheaded by Yabuli, achieved a breakthrough in imagenesis technology five years ago. Today, it's the source of all imagenae in Astropolis.
rows.speaker: Jerica

rows.text: Except... "imagenesis" is probably just a byproduct of her research.
rows.speaker: Jerica

rows.text: The Voracity Weaponization Project...
Yabuli's research target has always been the Voracity.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: She must have some deep connection to that underground leviathan Asat Pramad mentioned.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: With the IPC backing her, Yabuli must have made quite a few discoveries in Planarcadia.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: I wouldn't be surprised if she's developed a more potent "Shattered Star Bait" that could even attract the Voracity.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Isn't that exactly what you're looking for?
rows.speaker: Jerica

rows.text: I went ahead and booked an appointment for you. The operator was professional and polite, and based on Madam Yabuli's schedule, they set the meeting for six months from now.
rows.speaker: Jerica

rows.text: But let's be honest, you've never been the patient type, have you?
rows.speaker: Jerica

rows.text: Waiting has never worked when it comes to meeting IPC executives. I've learned that lesson far too many times.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Nothing beats showing up in person.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Funny you should say that. I've prepared a door for you. Care to guess where it leads?
rows.speaker: Jerica

rows.text: Well well, when will you be more honest?
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Takes one to know one.
rows.speaker: Jerica

rows.text: Looks like we've got a trip to make, [Trailblazer].
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Do you really believe that lady's nonsense?
Who cares if she's the real Aha or not...
We're fighting Oroboros here!
Haha, count me in!
*sniffle* The Troupe Master is actually Aha...
First time dealing with her nonsense?
You'll get used to it...
But Ahatopia needs us...
Unfortunately, this door no longer leads to Planarcadia.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: The tavern exists outside physical space, Ahatopia is encased in amber, and the door connecting them has been shut.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: A shell broken from the outside is nothing more than food. Let's trust everyone who stayed behind in Planarcadia.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: You're about to see your beloved Voracity.
rows.speaker: Helpless Fool

rows.text: Congratulations, my friend! You've been successfully selected as the sixteenth backup option in the Voracity Fishing Project!
rows.speaker: Helpless Fool

rows.text: Hoo! Alright, what do you need me to do? Sailor, first mate, or captain?
rows.speaker: Dewide Chungus

rows.text: Umm... bait.
rows.speaker: Helpless Fool

rows.text: You ate every last scrap of food in the tavern. If The Laughter really can't find any bait, well, you'll just have to take one for the team.
rows.speaker: Eager Fool

rows.text: You... you guys are actually treating me like a dish!?
rows.speaker: Dewide Chungus

rows.text: You're about to see your beloved Voracity. Why not cheer up a little?
rows.speaker: Helpless Fool

rows.text: Who will become the final victor?
rows.speaker: Busybody Fool

rows.text: A clash between Aeons, round two of the war of gods. Who will come out on top, The Laughter or the Voracity?
rows.speaker: Busybody Fool

rows.text: Welcome, all you clever folks, come place your bets!
rows.speaker: Busybody Fool

rows.text: I don't have high hopes for the ending of this play. But as a little consolation for the Troupe Master, I'll bet on "Win."
rows.speaker: Pessimistic Actor

rows.text: I'll bet on "lose." If The Laughter beats the Voracity, all's well that ends well.
rows.speaker: Shrewd Fool

rows.text: If The Laughter loses, at least I'll still win some prize money. That's what I call hedging my bets!
rows.speaker: Shrewd Fool

rows.text: We're only here temporarily...
rows.speaker: Planarcadia Refugee

rows.text: The Troupe Master's gondola has to be ready for open-sea voyaging. There's plenty of prep work still ahead. We need hands to inspect the keel, patch the hull, and take stock of the oars.
rows.speaker: Anxious Actor

rows.text: No worries, Fools are a hyperactive bunch. See? We've got plenty of hands to spare.
rows.speaker: Hearty Fool

rows.text: But we're only here temporarily from Planarcadia...
rows.speaker: Planarcadia Refugee

rows.text: Haha, loosen up. Even if you're a Fool who just walked through the tavern doors for the first time, the moment you walk through the doors, you're family!
rows.speaker: Hearty Fool

rows.text: Allow me to express my gratitude to you both for participating in the World in Canvas ritual. Lady Graphia, Miss Silver Wolf, thank you for your hard work.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: Phase one of the "painting" process has temporarily concluded.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: "Temporarily"? So you're not done milking us for free labor?
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: I was under the impression you were enjoying this, Miss Silver Wolf. Besides, walking away with Lady Graphia's "imagenesis" technique is a priceless reward in itself.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: What else would you like as payment?
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: Isn't it about time you handed back my data slice?
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Ah, you mean the "IPC Wolf"?
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: Stop calling it the IPC Wolf! You're ruining my street cred.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Of course. Consider your property returned.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: Jeez, you made multiple copies? Have you no basic decency?
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Exquisite skills are meant to be shared, just as the two of you once shared the art of "imagenesis" with me.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: My apologies, but I have to interrupt. Madam Pearl, you just said "temporarily concluded." Does that mean the crisis hasn't been fully averted?
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: That's correct. Leveraging the Amber Lord's gaze to seal the arcadia within a painting is merely a stopgap measure.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: A stopgap measure...? What, you wanna take it a step further and kill the husk?
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Even Aha couldn't take down this boss, and you're gonna try to get the first clear?
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Sick! But... isn't that a little greedy?
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: I wouldn't dare harbor such grand ambitions, but I am holding out a sliver of hope.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: "Weaponizing the husk" is merely temporarily on hold. Knowing how the Marketing Development Department operates, it won't be long before they orchestrate another "accident" to force the agenda back onto the table.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: So, you're preparing for a third "painting"?
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: Madam Pearl. As an artist, when I walk into this space, I see countless brushstrokes bleeding into one another. Colors layered, covered, and layered again... You've been relentless in your attempts to mimic my work.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: You are correct. But this is where the painting ends.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: I could mimic you a thousand times and replicate Worldbreaker Waves to perfection, yet there would still be that less-than-four-percent margin of error. I once assumed it was simply a lapse in my skill set...
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: But to my eyes, your painting skills have long since surpassed mine.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: I am glad you can admit that. The truth is, that four-percent gap stems from a variable that can never be imitated:
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: The raw emotion the artist commands and pours onto the canvas in the very instant of creation.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: A millennium later, even if you were to stand here yourself and take up the brush, you would merely be crafting another forgery.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: Indeed. To an artist, the catalyst for every work is singular. What I poured into my creations wasn't just technique, it was rage... and terror.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: Rage, and terror?
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Rage that I failed to stop Asat Pramad. Terror of knowing that the world's survival rested entirely on my shoulders, and fear that the World in Canvas ritual would not succeed.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: It was those intense emotions, sparked a millennium ago, that forged my bond with this world.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: Like the gaze of the Amber Lord, it was a human miracle that defies replication.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: And in realizing that, I found my own "four percent."
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: I felt the urge to leave my "mark" in places that cannot be predicted.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: An Intellitron having an "urge"? I thought you were a total logic-bot.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Hardly. Being one of the Ten Stonehearts means understanding risk. It's my entire job.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: But I've always operated by calculating and weeding out uncertainty, rather than letting it drive my work. I've spent my life mimicking masterpieces, but the real breakthroughs came from the things I couldn't quantify:
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: A detective throwing away billions of credits just to get the truth, a victim burning through fifteen years of their life to enact revenge on this arcadia...
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: ...And the Nameless of the Astral Express, trying bravely to be a sail against the storm.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: The strength of these emotions, erupting from the brink of despair, that's a variable no model can ever calculate.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: That's why you're done chasing "replication."
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: Exactly. My entire motif was to understand art, but I've realized art is far more than that which you put on canvas. My objective now is to paint a future for Planarcadia, not to just rehash some archaic, legendary feat.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: I am going to make sure that the plan to "weaponize the husk" and everyone behind it never stages a comeback.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: That's why, before the Express left, I added three "stray strokes" to this picture:
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: A dead woman, a killer, and a detective.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: As for whether fate will paint a scene in our favor...
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: Well, let's see if the Master of Elation is amused enough to let it happen.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: Skylight's open. Nice view, eh?
rows.speaker: Lighthouse

rows.text: Even the most spectacular views get old when you have to stare at them every single day.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: First Lodestar Tower, and now Yabuli's turf... I wonder what kind of surprises she has in store for us.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Alright, dear passenger! Stand firm, hold onto the handrails, and most importantly... relax.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: A plan? What plan?
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: The plan to secure the bait!
The plan to convince Yabuli!
Are we just going to waltz right in?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Did you forget? Yabuli is on Oswaldo's side!
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Heheh, you're in safe hands with me. With the greatest magician and her brilliant assistant on the job, what could possibly go wrong?
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: We're going to pay a visit to this old friend of ours whom we've never met in person... in true Elation fashion.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: A little performance that just so happens to reach her ears, showing her that we're the partners she should be doing business with.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: When the time comes, she'll come to us herself.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Well, you are Aha, after all.
Being an Aeon really comes in handy.
Fair point. Who dares to say no to Aha?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Is that what being an Aeon does to your ego?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Actually, [Trailblazer], before we head out, there's something I want to discuss with you.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: About this whole "I am Aha" business. I'd like to keep it a secret between just the two of us.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Plenty of people in the IPC covet the power of an Aeon, and Yabuli certainly won't be the last.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Having Fleming on our side doesn't do much. The IPC is like a bloated giant, whose head has lost control of its limbs.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: In the past, I wouldn't have minded playing along with their little games. But right now, that starving Voracity is running out of patience.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Alright, you have my word.
Going undercover. I like it.
Then it's a deal. If you go back on your word...
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: I'll invoke the authority of Elation to take away your belly button.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: That's just evil!
Can you take my appendix instead?
Heh heh. You're smart to be scared.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: I'm not haggling with you!
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: No time to lose. Let's head out and find a little appetizer for the Voracity!
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: This is the Life Sciences Institute?
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Feels more like a wispae theme park.
Kinda gives off a resort vibe.
Feels more like an amusement park than a research facility.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: I guess it matches the Astropolis aesthetic.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Makes sense. No technology can remain purely conceptual forever, and imagenesis is no exception.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Entertainment is the ultimate commodity. The Astral Express harvesting wishpower via Star Rail FEST is a case in point.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Once that value is visible, capital surges in like a tidal wave.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: As for what Yabuli does with that capital, that's a separate matter.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: What does she want to do with all that wishpower?
You should have been the Amber Lord.
Her "weaponizing the husk" proposal tells us that she's trying to see if she can control the leviathan.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Haha, masonry's way too much grunt work, not really my style.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: It's clear: Yabuli is no mere scholar. She's also an entrepreneur who wrings every drop of value from her assets.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: And where there's an entrepreneur, there's room to negotiate.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Let's press forward and see if we can find a staff member to secure us an introduction.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Oh? No welcome committee waiting at the door. I must say, I'm not used to this.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Scan complete. Welcome, esteemed guests, to the Life Sciences Institute!
rows.speaker: Bathyoculus

rows.text: "Welcome"? Did I hear that right?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Weird. Do I hear a fountain, music, and kids laughing?
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: There's something about the Life Sciences Institute that feels off.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Yeah, looks like someone beat us to it.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Dad, look! I've never seen the wispae run around like this before! Do they have a day off or something?
rows.speaker: Excited Kid

rows.text: Haha, glad we made the trip.
rows.speaker: Accompanying Father

rows.text: Ha, haha. Let's not be so loud in public, now.
rows.speaker: Accompanying Father

rows.text: There's still a lot we don't know about how imagenesis works. Tell the Control Team to send some people over. Can't let them escape the Ecological Exhibition Area!
rows.speaker: Distraught Maintenance Staff

rows.text: Wamp wah, so hard! Wamp wah, can't chew!
rows.speaker: Giant Wispae

rows.text: Ugh, this mess just has to happen on my shift.
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: Could you two step back? The wispae are pretty lively, but they're not aggressive. Just watch your heads. We don't want them bumping into you and ruining your day.
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: Are they staging a walkout or something?
How did that one climb so high?
Haha, the wispae have limited intelligence, so it's less of a walkout and more of a temper tantrum.
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: Ha, haha, yeah. We don't do imagenae shows here, but we can't help it either if they want to give us a show themselves.
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: You're pretty lucky. I've worked here a while and I've never seen these little guys so active.
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: Wamp wah, so hungry, so hot! Wamp wah, no going back!
rows.speaker: Boisterous Wispae

rows.text: Shh. Polite kids stay quiet when others are talking.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Oh, they quieted down! Was that magic?
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: H—How'd you do that? Are you two scholars from the Intelligentsia Guild?
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: No. Just a little parlor trick.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: How can I help you? Oh, I could give you a tour and show you what it's like to have imagenae and humans live side-by-side in harmony.
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: Give me the rundown on this place?
We need to see Ms. Yabuli.
This is the Wispae Eco-Park, run by the Life Sciences Institute. Five years ago, Ms. Yabuli cut the ribbon here, and introduced the very first artificial imagenae in Astropolis, λ-8983.
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: Since then, they've gone from lab experiments to household pets. And this place eventually went from a pop-science spot to a theme park where the wispae and the locals can just hang out.
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: I'm as confused as you are. I'm just a guide.
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: Usually, wispae get a bit hyper from Wishpower fluctuations, but that's about it.
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: Leaving their habitat, bouncing off the walls, and totally losing control? Yeah honestly, that doesn't really happen.
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: Please pass this message along. We're here to talk to Ms. Yabuli about a deal.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Department Head Yabuli? I don't recall her having any appointments today. Who are you two, anyway...?
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: This is [Trailblazer], the acting navigator of the Astral Express. And, you can call me Beatrice Mellanine.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Oh... uh... one moment please. I'll go report your arrival right away!
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: Looks like word got out about us turning the tables on the IPC at Lodestar Tower.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Still... the Wishpower flowing around here feels wrong.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: I'm curious. What kind of tech is Yabuli using to keep these imagenae going?
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Maybe that little one can give us the answer.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: It's so noisy over by the fountain. What's going on?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Wanna go to the fountain... catch some big wave...
rows.speaker: Restless Wispae

rows.text: Wamp wah, so cool, so refreshing!
rows.speaker: Restless Wispae

rows.text: Wamp wah, it climbed too high! It's gonna get all bruised up when it falls, wamp?
rows.speaker: Uneasy Wispae

rows.text: Eyelids... feel so heavy... Getting dizzy, wah...
rows.speaker: Restless Wispae

rows.text: Wamp, wah...
rows.speaker: Shocked Wispae

rows.text: Phew, that took some effort. You're safe, it's me.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Now let's look inside that black box of Yabuli's and see how Astropolis's Wishpower flows....
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: I see. So we're in the right place.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: I can sense an "artificial Phantasmoon"... right here in Astropolis.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: And we aren't the first guests to arrive, either.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: It's way livelier than I thought. Some of my old friends are here, too.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: "Old friends?"
Follow me. Let's go say hello.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: I'll fill you in on the way.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Wamp wah... dizzy...
rows.speaker: Giant Wispae

rows.text: Don't underestimate me! I've caught much bigger prey than you.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Looks like we beat the scholar here.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Perfect. We can talk about our findings.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: The Phantasmoon and leviathan are what sustain the Phantasmoon Games in Planarcadia.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Yabuli must've reverse-engineered the Phantasmoon Games, and built the same Wishpower loop in Astropolis.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: That's why imagenae can thrive here in Astropolis.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: How embarrassing for Aha.
The Tech Department knows their stuff.
Yabuli actually pulled that off?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: No wonder she thought she could weaponize the husk.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: But I'm dying to know exactly what she did. Does this woman have any idea of the consequences of her little experiment?
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Ah, there's the answer. It wasn't us setting off the wispae, it was our "old friend."
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: How unfortunate, Mr. Ashveil. Looks like our cover's blown.
rows.speaker: "Narrator"

rows.text: Haha, lucky it's you two who found us, Ms. Nihilux, [Trailblazer].
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: I knew it. The wispae weren't greeting us. They were just hungry for the smell of your arm.
rows.speaker: Kuchiba

rows.text: Ashveil? And Miss Kuchiba?
What are you doing here?
I'm here, too.
rows.speaker: "Narrator"

rows.text: We finished settling the refugees, so we decided—
rows.speaker: Kuchiba

rows.text: Madam Pearl sent us.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: This isn't a secret mission, and Pearl never asked us to keep it under wraps.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: That intel was: When the Strategic Investment Department still had jurisdiction over Ahatopia, Yabuli stole a certain something from Planarcadia.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: I don't know if it was flesh from the husk or a sample of the Abundance.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: But Yabuli used it to build this Wishpower loop in Astropolis. Maybe that's what gave her the confidence to pitch weaponizing the husk.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: We're here to snuff out her ambitions.
rows.speaker: Kuchiba

rows.text: Find the source of the danger... and destroy it.
rows.speaker: Kuchiba

rows.text: But what are you two doing here?
rows.speaker: Kuchiba

rows.text: Oh, there you are! Esteemed guests!
The wispae have all run away.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: What's this about an "artificial Phantasmoon"? Does it have anything to do with that "leviathan" the die mentioned?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: A Phantasmoon and a leviathan... It's almost like they're trying to recreate the Phantasmoon Games here.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: This isn't just a technical issue anymore. She must've pulled some real strings.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Finally found you, [Trailblazer] of the Astral Express, Ms. Mellanine...
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: If you don't mind, may I call you by that name?
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: ...Excuse me?
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: You don't know? Everybody here knows who you really are.
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: Don't look at me.
I heard that as soon as you and the Nameless stepped into Skycall Aery, Mr. Arita changed his mind. Then the whole city started buzzing with that name...
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: Dongfang Qixing! I mean, who else has that kind of pull, if not the descendant of one of the IPC's founding fathers alongside Fleming himself?
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: Whew.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Thank goodness, my belly button is safe.
I have informed Department Head Yabuli of your arrival, and she has tasked me with the honor of escorting you. Wait... there are five of you now?
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: They're... with me.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Bodyguard.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Assistant.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: ...And, uh, a pet.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Ahaha, a little mix up there?
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: Of course. For someone of your status, an entourage like this is practically low-key!
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: Please, follow me to the institute. Ms. Mellanine, Ms. Yabuli is quite interested in your "deal."
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: It's this easy?
Could this be a trap?
She's not mad that we jumped in and ruined her plan?
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Mad? No, no. Ms. Yabuli's not mad.
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: You'll understand when you meet her. To her, emotions are... a sensory illusion, a byproduct of biological functions.
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: Knowledge serves no one. It seeks only to reveal itself.
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: If you share her hunger for unearthing beautiful knowledge from this wretched world, you will find plenty of common ground.
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: Now, shall we?
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: Welcome, esteemed guests. Fasten your seatbelts, and get ready for a wild ride of discovery!
Hmm, a car stereo? Pretty fancy.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: Car stereo? I'm no simple piece of tech, pal.
rows.speaker: Racecar Imagenae

rows.text: Hehe, we produce a lot more than just wispae on our imagenae production lines.
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: All aboard, everyone!
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: And we've arrived at the Production Zone. Haha, I wouldn't have had the clearance to be here without you two.
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: What an elegant design! Imagenae are churned out day and night on the assembly line, forming the cornerstone of Astropolis's thriving economy.
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: For the longest time, "imagenesis" was just some unknown phenomenon on a faraway planet.
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: But only decades after the Technology Department settled in Planarcadia, Madam Yabuli recreated the Wishpower loop, to perfection. She always believed every phenomenon could be broken down into elegant principles.
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: Too bad the primitives back in Ahatopia, obsessed as they are with their little sketches, will never grasp that idea.
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: Oh, Ms. Mellanine, what's wrong? Are you tired from the walk?
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: Ah, haha. Don't worry, the classified sector is just up ahead. The Department Head will be seeing you there.
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: But she's right in the middle of a major experiment, so you'll need to give her a moment.
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: If either of you are interested in how the Technology Department produces imagenae, I can give you a tour of the process in the meantime.
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: Do we really have time for this?
Now that's ignorant. As the Fools say, the world is one big arcadia.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: I want to see exactly how much Yabuli knows about imagenesis.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: We can start with the raw material pressing phase. It's not my usual post, but I'll do my best to explain.
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: Before that, though, let me escort these three guests who aren't on the visitor list to the lounge.
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: A tour? Walking past glass cases is boring. I'm an experiential learner. [Trailblazer], let's go see the lines from the inside!
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: That... That's probably against the rules...
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: Rules? You're lecturing a descendant of the Dongfang family about rules? Think about it. Isn't the IPC's tech basically my family's tech?
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Oh no, no, you misunderstood! I just meant the imagenae production line can be a little dangerous, and you're so... important. Anyhow...
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: Anyhow that's a yes. Let's go.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: That was not a yes!
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: My apologies. The three of you, please wait here. I'll get a colleague to assist you... Esteemed guests, wait for me!
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: Look at the scale of this place. It puts Pearluxe Tower to shame, doesn't it?
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: I've got no intention of passing judgment on my boss.
rows.speaker: Kuchiba

rows.text: That neighbor of yours, though... Her behavior felt too calculated for simple curiosity. You think she figured something out?
rows.speaker: Kuchiba

rows.text: I must correct you. Not "neighbor," but "landlord."
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: And I've got no intention of passing judgment on my landlord.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: Hah. Right, let's keep the mission rolling.
rows.speaker: Kuchiba

rows.text: We'd better find our own way out before our long-winded guide tries to drag us to the break room for coffee.
rows.speaker: Kuchiba

rows.text: The vibe here is completely different from where we were.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: You've got a keen eye. If the Eco Park is the "face" of the Institute, the Production Zone here is the internal organs.
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: The R&D Zone further in, that's the "brain" of the Life Sciences Institute.
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: Please don't let anything go wrong...
Wait for me, honored guests!
In Planarcadia, the cores grow inside the imagenae. You've turned everything around... You're using cores to force the imagenae into existence.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Ahaha... aren't you well-informed, Ms. Mellanine?
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: The tour ends here.
Wait, oh, Madam Mastaka? What brings you here?
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: Finally. Someone who might actually have some answers.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: I'll take it from here, Scholar Fern. You may return to the laboratory.
O—Of course.
rows.speaker: Guide

rows.text: A pleasure to meet you. I am Mastaka, Madam Yabuli's personal Intellitron assistant. I trust you have enjoyed your time at the Life Sciences Institute.
This is lacking in sincerity, no? She's not gonna show up in person?
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Madam Yabuli is currently occupied with a highly critical experiment. Until her work concludes, I have assumed full authority over all Institute operations.
rows.speaker: Mastaka

rows.text: I shall review your proposal on her behalf to determine if it warrants the Technology Department Head's attention.
rows.speaker: Mastaka

rows.text: My apologies. That information is Grade-S classified. I cannot grant you clearance.
rows.speaker: Mastaka

rows.text: My apologies. That information is Grade-A classified. I cannot grant you clearance.
rows.speaker: Mastaka

rows.text: My apologies. That information is Grade-B classified. I cannot grant you clearance.
rows.speaker: Mastaka

rows.text: If everything is a secret, how are we supposed to negotiate? Is there anything here that isn't classified?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: The classified directory is also classified.
rows.speaker: Mastaka

rows.text: Hahaha, this Yabuli character sure has a sense of humor. Sending an obstinate Intellitron to stonewall us.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Drop the act, Yabuli. I know what you did in Planarcadia. I also know you can hear us, right now.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: ...Keyword detected. Updating visitor profile to: Interesting Mind.
rows.speaker: Mastaka

rows.text: The salvage and development operations on Planarcadia strictly adhere to the protocols of the "Worlds Reborn Initiative." Your accusations are unfounded.
rows.speaker: Mastaka

rows.text: I take my comment back. You have serious acting chops. I am tempted to poach you for my Actor Troupe. It takes talent to ignore the leviathan flesh sitting right out in the open on the assembly line.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Fleming has some nerve. If Qlipoth ever discovered you were tampering with this stuff on THEIR turf, THEY would drop the hammer on you.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Instinct drives leviathan flesh and {RUBY_B#the Voracity}essence{RUBY_E#} to attract one another. The Aeons used that exact trick to lure the "Voracity" into a trap.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Which means, the bait to hook THEM has been dangling in front of us the entire time. What the Technology Department wanted from Planarcadia was never the Phantasmoon Games, was it?
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: My apologies, that is also a trade secret. However, based on your input, I am restarting the negotiation process.
rows.speaker: Mastaka

rows.text: Acknowledged: The collaborator asks us to provide bait to lure a leviathan. Inquiry: What is the proposed compensation?
rows.speaker: Mastaka

rows.text: Yabuli, you want to uncover the secrets of the leviathans, but the plan to weaponize their remains was vetoed. Oswaldo's promises turned out to be hollow. We, however, can give you what you want.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: You want to experiment on leviathans.
Our goals do not conflict.
Doing business is about finding common ground while respecting differences.
We are not friends, but we are certainly not enemies either.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Here's an offer you cannot refuse.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Hand over the bait, and we will lure the Voracity out from the depths of Ahatopia for a practical experiment on an Aeonic scale.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Please wait. Deep reflection in progress. Simulating Madam Yabuli's decision tree.
rows.speaker: Mastaka

rows.text: Visitor profile updated to: Excellent Mind.
rows.speaker: Mastaka

rows.text: Biomass extracted from leviathans, leviathan derivatives, and from the remains of the Voracity husk is known as Leviathan Essence.
rows.speaker: Mastaka

rows.text: To hook the Voracity, one requires a high mass of concentrated Essence. The diluted derivatives here are insufficient.
rows.speaker: Mastaka

rows.text: Conclusion: Follow me to the depths of the Institute. Madam Yabuli will discuss our collaboration after the experiment.
rows.speaker: Mastaka

rows.text: Conclusion: Maintain current variables and continue.
rows.speaker: Mastaka Variant

rows.text: What experiment is this?
How many Mastakas are in this Institute?
Have you read Fluffy Across the Blue?
Retrieval of the 17th set of observation devices scheduled for one system hour from now.
rows.speaker: Mastaka Variant

rows.text: What are you trying to observe?
How is Planarcadia holding up?
Isn't Oswaldo just so annoying?
Security protocols modified.
rows.speaker: Mastaka Variant

rows.text: Where did you get the Leviathan Essence?
Have you heard of the School of Evolutionary Perfection?
How much do you make a month?
We have reached the Core Sector. Madam Yabuli's experiment is reaching its conclusion. Please, give her a moment.
rows.speaker: Mastaka

rows.text: [Trailblazer], do you recall our first encounter at Pearluxe Tower?
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: I don't remember. That was ages ago.
You mean, the birth of the mechatron?
I told you then that when people gaze upon lifeless things, they cannot help but project their own imagination onto them, envisioning them as living beings capable of thought and action.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: It was the Wishpower born from that empathetic "transference" that gave the imagenae life, fitting them with a mask of humanity.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: But in his design, Asat Pramad attempted to weaponize that same Wishpower, seeking to tame the husk to create and sustain his own army of monsters.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Did Yabuli take inspiration from that?
Did she want to teach the leviathan how to speak?
To satisfy her own curiosity toward leviathans, she began mimicking her enemies. Am I right, Mastaka?
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: My apologies. That is...
rows.speaker: Mastaka

rows.text: I shall take it from here, Mastaka. My apologies. I could not spare a moment for you until now.
Ms. Mellanine, the shape of your skull is truly exquisite. Might I take a photograph?
rows.speaker: Yabuli

rows.text: To be honest, I rarely encounter a cranial structure that begs so immediately to be opened. I am quite curious about the secrets hidden inside.
rows.speaker: Yabuli

rows.text: Don't even think about it.
Stop hiding in the shadows. Why not show yourself?
So you wanna fight?
The experiment is not yet finished. I merely split off a single neuron to greet you both in advance.
rows.speaker: Yabuli

rows.text: Oh no no, no need for theatrics. I simply harbor a fondness for human biomorphology.
rows.speaker: Yabuli

rows.text: I promise I would reassemble her perfectly. But it seems we lack the time, and you lack the inclination.
rows.speaker: Yabuli

rows.text: Getting back to business, Ms. Mellanine, you possess a great deal of information. Did the Strategic Investment Department feed you this?
rows.speaker: Yabuli

rows.text: My apologies. That is...
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Heh, I will take that as a yes. I already know why you are here. But tell me honestly, what is your stance on the Husk Weaponization initiative?
rows.speaker: Yabuli

rows.text: That plan is devoid of humanity.
I do not believe you are capable of controlling the Voracity.
The IPC is acting dangerously arrogant.
The proposal may seem enticing, but the cost is measured in the countless lives of Ahatopia. It's not a sacrifice. It's a slaughter.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Controlling a standard leviathan is a far cry from mastering the remains of the Voracity.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: The power of an Aeon is not something humanity was ever meant to command.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Furthermore, if even the geniuses could not achieve this, I don't see how you possibly could.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Me? Of course I cannot, nor can the Intelligentsia Guild.
rows.speaker: Yabuli

rows.text: But the IPC can. You are standing before the largest mega-corporation in the history of the universe, the most colossal organization humanity has ever assembled. Quantitative change eventually yields qualitative change. For a behemoth like the IPC, everything operates on a different scale.
rows.speaker: Yabuli

rows.text: Nanook can erase stars, and so can our own star-destroying arsenal. Yaoshi can breathe life into the dying and grant eternal youth, and our biotechnology can mirror that feat. It is merely a matter of time and cost.
rows.speaker: Yabuli

rows.text: Refine enough Leviathan Essence, and the husk is ours to command.
rows.speaker: Yabuli

rows.text: Have you ever taken a biology class? Apply a charge to a dead frog, and the limb twitches. It is all the same logic, merely a difference in complexity.
rows.speaker: Yabuli

rows.text: I never went to school.
That's just wishful thinking.
Well, now you know.
rows.speaker: Yabuli

rows.text: Many inventions that expanded human ability were dismissed as wishful thinking before they became reality.
rows.speaker: Yabuli

rows.text: For a follower of the Trailblaze, your thinking is pathetically conservative, child.
rows.speaker: Yabuli

rows.text: What gods can do, humanity can achieve as well. Given sufficient resources, nothing is impossible.
rows.speaker: Yabuli

rows.text: I know you do not believe me, but beneath the central pipeline, I have already birthed a Phantasmoon far more controllable than the original.
rows.speaker: Yabuli

rows.text: And that is only the beginning. Oroboros's husk has awakened. Once I bind myself to THEIR flesh and blood, I will claim THEIR wisdom.
rows.speaker: Yabuli

rows.text: An Aeon becoming an asset of the IPC. That will be an achievement without equal.
rows.speaker: Yabuli

rows.text: How long will her experiment take?
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Estimated completion is within one system hour.
rows.speaker: Mastaka

rows.text: What are those pipes?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: The blood vessels and nerves of the Life Sciences Institute. Energy, data... everything the Institute needs flows through them to every corner of the facility, ultimately converging here.
rows.speaker: Mastaka

rows.text: Does that include the Leviathan Essence?
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: That is classified.
rows.speaker: Mastaka

rows.text: The monument before you is engraved with the School of Evolutionary Perfection's vision for intelligent life.
rows.speaker: Mastaka

rows.text: Feel free to read it if you are interested.
rows.speaker: Mastaka

rows.text: There are so many of you!
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: Negative. There are significant variations in performance between us. My performance is the highest.
rows.speaker: Mastaka

rows.text: Really? Is that all you can say?
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: My apologies...
rows.speaker: Mastaka

rows.text: That is also classified. Yeah, I got the gist.
rows.speaker: [Trailblazer]

rows.text: If Aha heard you say that, THEY would undoubtedly say...
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Yabuli, just give up.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Thousands of Amber Eras ago, it took the collective might of several Aeons, at the cost of countless star systems and the disappearance of one Aeon, just to dismember and seal the Voracity.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Your bravado is merely the arrogance of a naive child who picks up a torch and claims to have mastered fire.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: That entity you think holds the key to the truth? It is nothing of the sort. If you persist on this path, it will culminate only in a belated retribution.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Hand over the Leviathan Essence. It's not too late.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Do you truly hold yourselves in such high regard?
rows.speaker: Yabuli

rows.text: That conversation was simply me sharing my vision. I never intended to make any deal with you.
rows.speaker: Yabuli

rows.text: Because, if you die on Ahatopia, the IPC will inevitably restart my initiative.
rows.speaker: Yabuli

rows.text: Even if there is a one-in-a-billion chance you manage to reseal the husk, my plan will remain on the Board's list of contingencies so long as the war among the Aeons looms.
rows.speaker: Yabuli

rows.text: So, there is no negotiation?
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Why not? Let's negotiate.
rows.speaker: Yabuli

rows.text: Bring Aha here. Have THEM take the Voracity's place on my operating table, and I will concede to all your demands.
rows.speaker: Yabuli

rows.text: You really are incorrigible.
You got my hopes up for nothing.
I suggest you take her advice.
Ms. Mellanine, don't play the saint and lecture me on the error of my ways.
rows.speaker: Yabuli

rows.text: I am not lecturing. I am offering you a chance to change.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: If you wish to continue admiring my work, I don't mind giving the two of you a tour. But if you are here to cause a scene...
rows.speaker: Yabuli

rows.text: I shall be forced to have you removed.
rows.speaker: Yabuli

rows.text: So, will you two make the smart choice?
rows.speaker: Yabuli

rows.text: I give up. Remember, you chose this path yourself.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Since you are so desperate to meet Aha, I'll grant your wish.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: ▄▄▄You█▀▄You▀▄Yooou▄
rows.speaker: The Mastakas

rows.text: Whoa, what did you do?
Finally, some peace and quiet.
Now you know who you are dealing with.
No, [Trailblazer]. I didn't do anything.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: Someone beat me to it. Yabuli is in trouble.
rows.speaker: Nihilux

rows.text: A dead woman, a killer, and a detective...
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: You're not speaking in metaphors, are you?
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Lady Graphia, I'd like to ask you a question.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: What is the most surefire way to destroy an unfinished painting once and for all?
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: Burning it.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: That's thorough indeed. But what if the canvas itself cannot be destroyed?
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: Then you ensure the artist can never hold a brush again.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: Precisely. "Weaponizing the Voracity" is a perilous endeavor that needs to be stopped, but I also have a duty to protect the {RUBY_B#Planarcadia}"canvas."{RUBY_E#}
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: My rationale: Find a new approach, even if it means choosing between the {RUBY_B#Leviathan Essence}"paint"{RUBY_E#} and the {RUBY_B#Yabuli}"artist."{RUBY_E#}
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: My conclusion: Kill Yabuli.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: Tsk. Are you the real Pearl, or some Masked Fool wearing her face?
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Taking the head of an IPC executive from several star systems away? Not even SAM would talk a game that big.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Not to mention that you are currently in Planarcadia.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: I cannot intervene personally, so Yabuli's execution is not "surefire" yet. Given the current variables, the probability of killing her stands at 92.7 percent.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: ...You say that like you're calculating stock market odds.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: And the one executing this mission is the "killer" you mentioned.
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: Kuchiba. Security Officer of the Department of Aberration Defense.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: We have already thoroughly covered the subject of the new Herald of Death and the Lord Ravager.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: Next, I think we should talk a bit more about you, Security Officer.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: ...Looks like you've been keeping tabs on me.
rows.speaker: Kuchiba

rows.text: During the construction of Inkford Hermitage, I uncovered a portrait wedged between the walls of the old Murata residence.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: The painting depicts a wicked beast priestess that a member of the Murata family saw in a dream. Unlike her bloated attendants, this priestess was slender, clad in black, and bore the exact likeness of a human woman. And her face...
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: ...Looked just like mine, yes?
rows.speaker: Kuchiba

rows.text: That member of the Murata family was a friend, of sorts. I taught her how to embrace her inner beast and confront her desires to withstand the Weathering Curse.
rows.speaker: Kuchiba

rows.text: A pity. People have a habit of hunting down dangerous animals.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: Are you planning to lock me up? I'm sure you can do it, with your resources.
rows.speaker: Kuchiba

rows.text: No. At the very least, in the decade or so you've served as Security Officer, you have performed your duties flawlessly.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: I am only curious. Why did you join the Department of Aberration Defense? And why go out of your way to warn us?
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: The answer is simple.
rows.speaker: Kuchiba

rows.text: Because I'm fond of {RUBY_B#food}humans{RUBY_E#}.
rows.speaker: Kuchiba

rows.text: Sometime prior, she approached me, offering to intervene in the current Phantasmoon Games.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: So I played along. Out of all the unfolding possibilities, I chose the path that offered us the greatest tactical advantage.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: You mean the greatest advantage for you.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Now I get why you brought the third-rate detective along. He's your fail-safe to keep that monster-in-disguise in check.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: You're not worried he'll get chewed up too?
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: Ashveil caged a beast inside his own body. The Beast-Binding Nail the Xianzhou made for him is one of the very few things that can actually counter a leviathan.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: But I didn't choose him solely for his capabilities. More crucially, out of all the Supplicants, he's the only one whose behavior is entirely predictable.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: He is a former Ranger leader harboring a wolf within, yet bound by an absolute code of justice. His one true goal is to preserve the greater good. That's not speculation, it's the conclusion I've reached.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: In my design, predictable justice eclipses all other variables.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: Sounds pretty lofty, but you're still just using him.
rows.speaker: Silver Wolf

rows.text: It's about putting the right person just where they need to be. Conclusion: I trust him.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: And what about yourself? What role do you intend to play in this grand scheme?
rows.speaker: Graphia

rows.text: The brush has already done all that it must. There is no need for me to take the stage. I choose to stay here.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: They should've arrived at the Life Sciences Institute by now. Given the current variables, the probability of Yabuli's death is 95.4 percent. Now I just need to oversee the remaining 4.6 percent.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: And deliver the final brushstroke.
rows.speaker: Pearl

rows.text: Ahem. Miss Kuchiba, your headphones are leaking.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: My apologies. I suddenly feel ravenous.
rows.speaker: Kuchiba

rows.text: Didn't we just eat?
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: Forget it. Next time we infiltrate a hostile area, mute your phone.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: Before we proceed, I need to confirm something. What was your assignment from Pearl?
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: I assumed you knew.
rows.speaker: Kuchiba

rows.text: I do. But I never heard it from you.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: I'm to provide cover for you, investigate Yabuli's background, and locate the Leviathan Essence she has hidden away.
rows.speaker: Kuchiba

rows.text: Then, either secure it or destroy it. I'm to use my own discretion for the rest.
rows.speaker: Kuchiba

rows.text: Own discretion. That's exactly what I wanted to ask about. What if innocent people get in the way?
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: Our definitions of "innocent" might differ. I'm a Security Officer. You are a detective...
rows.speaker: Kuchiba

rows.text: ...and under that mask of yours, a Galaxy Ranger.
rows.speaker: Kuchiba

rows.text: So that little secret is all out in the open.
rows.speaker: "Narrator"

rows.text: Mister N, I told you not to tag along. You could've stayed outside as backup.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: Mr. Ashveil, I was a Ranger myself for decades.
rows.speaker: "Narrator"

rows.text: The stench of Leviathan Essence... I know it all too well. Those tainted by it rarely return to normal.
rows.speaker: "Narrator"

rows.text: I'm certain that it's right under this production line. If you two go down there, you might not make it back out in one piece.
rows.speaker: "Narrator"

rows.text: Are you proposing a change of plan, or trying to convince us to turn back?
rows.speaker: Kuchiba

rows.text: Neither. Just like Mr. Ashveil, I simply want to know...
rows.speaker: "Narrator"

rows.text: ...If things go sideways, Miss Kuchiba, what choice will you make?
rows.speaker: "Narrator"

rows.text: I will complete the mission. What other option is there?
rows.speaker: Kuchiba

rows.text: Relax, Detective. We still have you to keep things in check, don't we.
rows.speaker: Kuchiba

rows.text: Besides, Pearl sent us backup.
rows.speaker: Kuchiba

rows.text: The bootleg Silver Wolf. Still operational, I see.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: "I am the personal AI of the great Madam Pearl. Mission: Hack the production line. Estimated time: Two minutes and fifty-two seconds."
rows.speaker: IPC Wolf

rows.text: I can't believe Pearl kept that thing around.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: I'm not surprised. She's planning to mass-produce them.
rows.speaker: Kuchiba

rows.text: With that, she left ahead of them. Before the trio disappeared into the darkness, the scene fell into an all-too-familiar silence.
rows.speaker: "Narrator"

rows.text: Everything of importance had been said. All that remained were the echoes of footsteps and the lingering doubts in their minds.
rows.speaker: "Narrator"

rows.text: ...Mr. Ashveil, we are probably thinking the same thing.
rows.speaker: "Narrator"

rows.text: If I take off my mask, I'm still a Galaxy Ranger.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: But if you take off your mask, Miss Kuchiba, then what are you?
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: Peel back the polished veneer, and you will always find something rotten underneath.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: Look on the bright side. It's probably not as bad as on Vonwacq.
rows.speaker: "Narrator"

rows.text: No, Mister N. Vonwacq was an isolated experiment. Just some lunatic tinkering in his basement, scheming to regress the entire universe into apes.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: But this, this is a mass-production line.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: Seventy-eight "Lighthouses." Seventy-eight... leviathans. The masses revere these monstrosities as heroes, place their faith in them, worship them...
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: And not even "Lighthouse" himself knows the truth.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: Let's say he did know. What difference would it make?
rows.speaker: Kuchiba

rows.text: We split up. Production logs, raw material pipelines, everything. Scour the place for anything useful.
rows.speaker: Kuchiba

rows.text: We have to locate the Leviathan Essence if we want to be of help to anybody.
rows.speaker: Kuchiba

rows.text: She's playing the detective better than you are at the moment.
rows.speaker: "Narrator"

rows.text: ...I'm aware.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: Look at this. On Inherited-State Knowledge: A Phylogenetic Interpretation of leviathan Information Structures. Timestamp: 2145 AE.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: Another ancient monster.
rows.speaker: "Narrator"

rows.text: You understood that title?
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: "2145" was the only part I got.
rows.speaker: "Narrator"

rows.text: "For eons, humanity has projected its search for knowledge outward, tirelessly charting the borders of the known. Yet they have all been blind to a profound truth: Knowledge possesses another, far more ancient pathway, one that turns inward."
rows.speaker: Yabuli

rows.text: "The geniuses obsess over controlling the final endpoint of knowledge. Conversely, at the dawn of the Amber Era, even before the Dusk Wars, pre-dating the birth of Aeons and the era of the primordial nouspores, leviathans were already entrenched at the absolute beginning."
rows.speaker: Yabuli

rows.text: The concept is easy enough to grasp.
rows.speaker: Ashveil

rows.text: "leviathans' comprehension of the cosmos is not communicated through crude text or imagery. It is branded directly into their genetic code."
rows.speaker: Yabuli

rows.text: "These entities, dwarfing entire nebulae and devouring stars, have transcended the petty confines of human intellect. Through endless consumption and evolution, they pass down an inheritance of eldritch, other-than-human wisdom."
rows.speaker: Yabuli
